items.reason: protect.c:9 `#define FLT_LOG_LEN     16` is the fault-log length used as a ring buffer size in `flt_log[flt_idx++ & (FLT_LOG_LEN - 1)]` (stores fault codes).

protect.c:13 `static const float k_trip_a = 15.0f; /* A rms, overload trip */` is compared in `prot_slow()` as `if (i_rms > k_trip_a)` to decide overload trip after a hold time, matching the software overload trip level. literal is RMS current in A.

protect.c:14 `static const unsigned short ol_hold_ms = 5000; /* overload ride-through */` is used as the time above `k_trip_a`: `if (++ol_ms >= ol_hold_ms) { inv_off(); ... }` where `ol_ms` is decremented/incremented in `prot_slow()` assumed 1 ms cadence. So it is the overload action delay window in ms.

protect.c:34 inline threshold `if (a > 21.2f)` where `a` is `abs(i_pk)`; on exceed it immediately does `inv_off()` and logs `FLT_OC`. This is a fast peak-current comparator threshold for over-current, corresponding to the hardware peak-current limit rule conceptually. Value is in A (peak), not RMS; rule mapping is to `iout_pk_limit` as the only matching limit.

protect.c:49 inline `if (vo_rms < 0.9f * VO_NOM)` logs `FLT_BRN` (brownout). The constant `0.9f` is a dimensionless fraction of `VO_NOM` defining a lower operating threshold; since the spec rule for a regulated band edge would be separate constants (e.g., vout_lo) but this is a relative fraction, it does not map directly to any provided rule id.
protect.c:54 inline `if (retry < 3)` uses literal `3` as the maximum restart/retry count for `prot_restart()`.
protect.c:55 inline `delay_ms(500);` uses literal `500` as a restart delay in ms before calling `inv_on()` again; this is not specifically the overload delay or any other named spec rule.
FW_VER_MAJ (line 19) is firmware major version.
VIN_LO_XFER (line 22) is the input voltage threshold ("go to battery below this, Vrms"); corresponds to vin_min.
VIN_HI_XFER (line 23) is the input voltage threshold ("go to battery above this, Vrms"); corresponds to vin_max.
VBUS_REF (line 26) is PFC bus regulation target in volts; corresponds to the DC bus regulation setpoint (vbus_set).
VO_NOM (line 29) is the nominal output voltage (Vrms); corresponds to vout_set.
VO_TOL (line 30) is the fractional regulation band tolerance (±VO_TOL) used to form the band edges; it is not itself an edge.
VO_HI (line 31) defines the upper output regulation band edge via VO_NOM*(1+VO_TOL); corresponds to vout_hi.
IO_RATED (line 32) is rated output current (A rms, stated 1500 VA/120 V); corresponds to iout_rated.
I_TRIP_RMS (line 33) is overload shutdown threshold (A rms); corresponds to iout_trip (software timed trip level).
TMR_LD (line 36) is PWM period register value ("PWM period, 25 kHz carrier"); corresponds to pwm_period (counts).
DB_CNT (line 37) is dead-time count register ("300 us dead time"); corresponds to pwm_deadband (counts).
K_P (line 40) is the voltage-loop proportional gain; corresponds to vloop_kp.
K_I (line 41) is the voltage-loop integral gain per control ISR; corresponds to vloop_ki.
VBAT_NOM (line 44) is the battery string nominal voltage; corresponds to vbat_nom.
VBAT_CUT (line 45) is end-of-discharge / low-battery cutoff voltage; corresponds to vbat_cutoff.
UART_BAUD (line 48) is the front-panel/RS-232 UART baud rate; no rule id provided for this.
PIN_BYP_RELAY (line 49) is a GPIO pin number for the static bypass relay drive.
ADC_FULL = 4095.0f is the ADC full-scale count for the sense chain (12-bit converter). It sets the full-scale count used in scaling, not a physical V/A limit by itself.
DAC_FULL = 4095 is the comparator reference DAC full-scale code used to form comparator DAC thresholds.
VBUS_FS = 498.3f is documented as 'V at ADC full scale' for the DC bus divider (1.5 M / 10 k). This matches the rule vbus_fs.
K_VS = (VBUS_FS / ADC_FULL) is 'V per count' for the bus ADC scaling. This corresponds to vbus_scale.
VBAT_FS = 168.0f is 'V at ADC full scale' for the battery divider (499 k / 10 k). This matches vbat_fs.
VO_FS_PK = 501.6f is 'peak V at +/- half scale' for the output voltage sensing (mid-rail biased). This matches vout_fs_pk.
IO_FS_PK = 33.0f is 'peak A at +/- half scale' for output current sensing (mid-rail biased). This matches iout_fs_pk.
CMP_DAC_HI = 3364 is the 'positive overcurrent trip code' for the comparator reference DAC. This maps to the positive hardware peak-current limit DAC code (iout_pklim_dac_hi).
CMP_DAC_LO = (DAC_FULL - CMP_DAC_HI) forms the 'negative' comparator trip code from the full-scale and the high code. This maps to iout_pklim_dac_lo.
